_what: Items the director read and refused on ISMS-IA. A rejection is the one disposition no generated artifact carries, so the standing list must be read by anything that promotes. approve-grounded-items.mjs reads this file by content id.
_every_entry_names_its_artifact_and_its_: A REPORT NUMBER IS NOT AN IDENTITY -- see the ISMS-F file for the incident that established this. Every entry carries an `artifact` and an `item_id`.

rounds.note: Writer claude-opus-5. All 19 accepted. The director notes the items are consistently scenario judgements, which is what an Internal Auditor exam should test.

Writer claude-sonnet-5-5. 3 of 13 rejected, all for IMPLAUSIBLE DISTRACTORS rather than a wrong anchor: options rejectable on common sense, a strawman, a repeated key. The PROMPT-127 s4 writer note addresses exactly this and applies to BOTH models.

Writer claude-sonnet-5-5. One reject, and it is a CROSS-WRITER duplicate the in-run gate could not see: both writers wrote the same tasks from the same prompt and neither artifact could see the other. check-cross-artifact-duplicates.mjs now exists and independently flags this pair at 67 percent key-word share.

Writer claude-sonnet-5-5. THREE dispositions, and the distinction is the point: 3 rejects are the writer's fault, 7 are duplicates of items already live, and 7 are twins within the round. The director ruled the tripwire NOT tripped because only the first 3 are a writer defect -- 5% of 60 -- and a writer is never shown what the bank already tests on its anchor.

Writer claude-sonnet-5-5. ZERO quality rejects. All 8 rejections duplicate a live item, so the whole of the waste is now duplication rather than item quality -- which is what the PROMPT-130 s3 semantic judge is for.
Writer claude-opus-5 on task 3.7 alone, reverted by the PROMPT-128 s4 tripwire. All 3 accepted: 3 of 4 survived where Sonnet had produced 0 of 4 in R3.

Writer claude-sonnet-5-5. THE JUDGE'S 12 FLAGS WERE ALL UPHELD -- the director would have called every one. Its single miss (65362731 against 3da7fa4a) is a CROSS-ANCHOR pair, which a same-anchor judge cannot see; PROMPT-131 s3 adds key-term neighbours for exactly that.

rejections.why: RULED reject (PROMPT-127 s1): two of the three distractors are not answers anyone would pick ("visit calendar the certification body sets", "headcount"). That is recall with filler.
RULED reject (PROMPT-127 s1): same key text as 95bc0088, which the solver rejected. One distractor ("the cheapest controls available") is not a plausible answer.

RULED reject (PROMPT-127 s1): two options both name top management, and the fourth ("only after a certification body issued major nonconformities") is a strawman. The item is answered by eliminating the strawman, not by knowing 9.3.

RULED reject (PROMPT-128 s1): it tests the same 9.3.3 point, with the same key, as Opus 22090360, and it is the plain-recall version of it. Stem overlap is 41 percent so no stem rule sees it; the anchor-and-key signal added in PROMPT-128 s2 measures 67 percent and flags it.
RULED reject (PROMPT-129 s1): Terminology trap: it turns on "audit evidence" against "objective evidence" inside the definition. That is pedantry, not audit skill.
RULED reject (PROMPT-129 s1): Plain recall ("relevant management") with a "combined audit" veneer. Nothing in it tests a combined audit.

RULED reject (PROMPT-129 s1): Its key ("not acceptable; someone else should audit") contradicts what the bank already teaches on independence (6b73a816, df1baea4: proceed with measures against bias when no one else is available). The stem does not say whether anyone else is available, so a learner cannot tell which lesson applies.
